rebuttal_or_critique: While I acknowledge the concerns of my colleagues regarding food inflation at 8.69%, I maintain that monetary policy is a blunt instrument for supply-side shocks. With core inflation at a benign 3.10%, the real policy rate is already sufficiently restrictive. Maintaining a 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance risks over-tightening and unnecessarily constraining the 6.80% GVA growth momentum. A shift to 'neutral' better reflects the current macroeconomic reality where the output gap is only marginally positive at 0.40%, and it provides the MPC with the necessary flexibility to respond to incoming data without signaling an overly hawkish bias that may dampen private investment.
